clue.text: Expression of resignation by plodder, one quick to know the score

definitions.text: one quick to know the score

parts.note: a sigh is the sound of someone giving up or accepting their lot
a plodder treads heavily along, so is a treader

explanation.surface: A weary walker gives a sigh of resignation, contrasted with someone quick on the uptake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The score' here is printed music, not a sporting result or a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who can play from printed music at first glance grasps the score at once.

clue.text: One could accommodate members of the nut

definitions.text: One could accommodate members of the nut

parts.words: One could accommodate members of the nut
parts.note: nut is slang for head, so the members of the head's team are a school's teachers, and this is the room set aside for them

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the nut' as the head, i.e. the head teacher: the people under the head are the teaching staff, and a school keeps a common room for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's common room for teachers houses the people who work under the head teacher.

clue.text: Sort of plant to have sticker on?

definitions.text: Sort of plant to have sticker on?

parts.words: Sort of plant to have sticker on?
parts.note: a sticker is a sticky substance like chewing gum, and a plant big enough to carry it is a tree

explanation.walkthrough: The eucalyptus is called this because its bark oozes sticky resin; the clue jokes that it is a plant with something sticky on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus, which exudes a sticky resin, is commonly named after that sticky stuff.

clue.text: Play for time, giving office worker zero increase

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
zero is the figure 0, read as the letter O
a rise is an increase, as in a pay rise

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker stalls because they have been given no pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or stall in order to gain time is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Course dealt with various poems

indicators.note: various signals the letters of the word poems being arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A literature course covered a range of poems.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous English racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Welshman tells fibs, according to the papers

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
to tell fibs is to lie, giving lies

explanation.surface: The newspapers report that a man from Wales is a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily newspapers are collectively called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Institute's commendation quietly ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the letter for quietly is left out of the word for commendation

parts.note: commendation is praise
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An institute's words of praise were quietly overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Institute stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something, such as a question or a fund, is to set it up or bring it up.

clue.text: Sun attracts enthusiastic throng

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun or Sunday
a warm welcome is an enthusiastic one

explanation.surface: Sunshine draws an eager crowd outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense crowd moving together is a synonym for a throng.

clue.text: Problem with spine hit last week?

definitions.text: Problem with spine hit last week?

parts.words: Problem with spine hit last week?
parts.note: a back injury, also read as a record that was a hit last week and has since fallen down the charts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disc' is also a record, and a hit record from last week has slipped down the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced spinal cartilage pad is a common back injury; read playfully, it is a record that has dropped down the charts.

clue.text: Perplexed and stymied if sent the wrong way

indicators.note: sent the wrong way signals that the letters of stymied and if are misdirected into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone blocked and sent off in the wrong direction is understandably puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being baffled or bewildered is to be left perplexed.

clue.text: Man facing surgery with nothing to lose — hopeless state

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for nothing is dropped from the word for surgery

parts.note: surgery is an operation
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man about to undergo an operation feels he has nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops the first O of OPERATION, leaving PERATION; 'facing' just sets DES beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter loss of hope is the condition described as a hopeless state.

clue.text: Facts about English sailors in hellish situation

indicators.note: about means the word for facts is placed around the other letters

parts.note: info is short for information, facts
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: Information about English seamen caught in a dreadful situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing fire or scene of chaos resembles hell, the meaning of this Italian-derived word.

clue.text: There's no scoring with these girls

definitions.text: There's no scoring with these girls

parts.words: There's no scoring with these girls
parts.note: young unmarried women who reject advances, also cricket overs in which no runs are scored

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'maiden' over is one from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried young women are maidens, and a maiden over in cricket has no runs scored.

clue.text: Somewhere to swim at far end of the town

parts.note: a pool is somewhere to swim

indicators.note: far end of picks out the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone describes where to swim: at the far end of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: POOLE is a coastal town in Dorset, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Poole is a seaside town and port in Dorset, England.

clue.text: Sort of earthenware in no store surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of in no store come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A type of pottery is surprisingly not stocked in any shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, dense white ceramic once sold as a type of earthenware carries this trade name.

clue.text: Defeat finished with one of the strikers in the box

parts.note: something finished is over

parts.words: one of the strikers in the box
parts.note: a match is one of the sticks struck in a matchbox

explanation.surface: A football defeat is over, with one of the team's strikers in the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers in the box' suggests footballers in the penalty area, but they are matches in a matchbox.
explanation.definitionFit: To be too strong for an opponent and beat them is to overmatch them.

clue.text: Old female darts across motorway, getting out of bounds

indicators.note: across means the word for darts stretches over the motorway letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to dart about is to flit, giving flits
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: An elderly woman dashes across a motorway, going where she should not.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; its number 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A place you are forbidden to enter is off limits, or out of bounds.

clue.text: A dramatic incident follows mother producing sword

indicators.note: follows means the later words come after the word for mother

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a scene is a dramatic incident, an outburst

explanation.surface: A mother makes a scene, and someone produces a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade of patterned Damascus steel was prized as a Damascene sword.

clue.text: I sat befouled with mud in sports field

indicators.note: befouled suggests the letters of I sat and mud being messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sat in the mud and got filthy at the sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports arena with tiered seating around the playing field is a stadium.

clue.text: Terrorists in Jerusalem — a fiasco

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are hidden in the words Jerusalem a fiasco

explanation.surface: A terror attack in Jerusalem turns into a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised criminal gang operating through intimidation and violence, loosely called terrorists here.

clue.text: Vegetables spoil — lines of them in garden

parts.note: to spoil is to mar
vegetables are planted in rows, lines in a garden

explanation.surface: Vegetables go off, rows of them in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: MARROWS are large courgette-like gourds, a staple of British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Large green squash grown in British gardens are known as marrows.

clue.text: Relief money about to be collected in pubs for natives

indicators.note: collected in means the reversed relief word is gathered inside the word for pubs

parts.note: inns are pubs

indicators.note: about means the word for relief money is turned round

parts.note: aid is relief money

explanation.surface: Relief money is about to be collected in pubs for the native people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses AID to DIA, which 'collected in' puts inside INNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous inhabitants, of India or the Americas, are called Indians.

clue.text: Man is buried under lair

indicators.note: buried under puts the word is below the word for lair in this down clue

parts.note: an animal's den is its lair

explanation.surface: A man is buried beneath an animal's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis is a male first name.

clue.text: The female graduate in a wealthy old place

parts.note: she refers to a female person
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A female graduate lives in a rich historic place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Sheba came from this ancient kingdom, famed for its riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical kingdom whose queen visited Solomon was famously rich.

clue.text: Rifle in one market at the front

indicators.note: at the front means the word for market goes before the other pieces

parts.note: a mart is a market
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Searching through one market stall at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a verb meaning to search, but it is the gun: the Martini-Henry was a Victorian army rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Martini-Henry was a breech-loading British army rifle, shortened to Martini.

clue.text: Temperate part of the globe

definitions.meaning: temperate means self-restrained, especially sexually or in drinking
a part of the globe is one of the great landmasses such as Europe or Asia

explanation.definitionFit: Self-restrained is continent as an adjective; one of Earth's great landmasses is a continent as a noun.

clue.text: Stars love performing outside science institution

indicators.note: outside means the love and performing letters sit around the science institution letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
on means performing, as an actor on stage
RI is the Royal Institution, a London science body

explanation.surface: Star performers in love, working outside a science institute.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Hunter is a famous group of stars.

clue.text: Shows compassion for missy — she apt to break down

indicators.note: to break down signals that the letters of missy and she apt fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: Someone feels for a young lady who is apt to burst into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel and express sorrow for someone's suffering is to sympathise with them.
